correctness.rationale: For every N,d, diagonal central/modulation invariance makes monomial exponent weights obey N|(u+v-s-t) and m|(v-t). Below min(N,2m), balancing plus |v-t|<m proves phase constancy. Under full S1, balance is unconditional and threshold 2m. Explicit Q_d and cited I_N attain sharp degrees for all positive amplitudes; order-two antipodal exception is treated. Reconstructed proof applies at N=2 and N>2. Finite checks (3016 assertion groups) confirm formulas but do not replace congruence proof.

value.rationale: It locates the exact nongeneric blind-spot degree where finite-Heisenberg low-degree invariants begin detecting phase for any two-sparse cyclic signal, with a number-theoretic dependence on support separation. The phase-invisibility degree grows unboundedly (2p in prime projective dimension), clarifying why generic degree-six orbit recovery does not offer uniform sparse guarantees. Exact sharp obstructions can guide invariant-feature design and sparse orbit recovery; not a gratuitous isolated count.
